education.detail: Law major; two-year member of Army sprint football (2010-11).

career.detail: Tim's bio calls older brother Mike "the current Athletic Intern" (a post often held by new graduates before branch school).

awards.title: All-CSFL first team (Collegiate Sprint Football League)
awards.detail: Led Army in rushing (48.8 ypg; 293 yards on 59 carries, five TDs); 103 yards and a TD v. Princeton; scored in the season-finale win at Navy.

bioAdditions: Mike played sprint football (players under a weight limit) at West Point. He wore No. 5 and was listed as a linebacker on the 2011 roster as a senior from Fairfax, Va., and Robinson Secondary. In 2010, his first season, he was All-CSFL first team and led Army in rushing at 48.8 yards a game. He scored in his first two games, at RPI and Mansfield, ran for 103 yards and a touchdown against Princeton and scored in the season-finale win at Navy, which decided the league title. His bio calls him a law major, the son of Dan and Ann Meier, and says his father played football at NC State and his brother Tim was on the team. At Robinson he was first-team all-district and all-region and played in the Virginia state all-star game (S1). His brother Tim's bio says Mike later served as Army's athletic intern (S2).

openQuestionsResolved.question: Confirm whether he is the Mike Meier named Washington Post All-Met honorable mention (running back, Robinson, 2006).
openQuestionsResolved.answer: Very likely. His West Point bio says he was first-team all-district and all-region at Robinson and played in the state all-star game, and he played running back at Army. That fits a 2006 All-Met honourable mention, though no source states the All-Met honour outright.

openQuestionsNew: Branch and later career after Fort Sill (presumably Field Artillery) not found; DVIDS search pages returned empty, and the "1st Lt. Michael Meier" in DVIDS is a Marine VMI graduate, a different man.
